alt: A grid of compressed cells holding how many rectangles cover each one, beside a table of the original width of each column and original height of each row. The sum moves down the grid one row at a time, multiplying each covered cell's width by its row's height and adding the result to two running totals: the area covered at least once and the area covered at least twice.

steps.caption: The depths from the last figure sit on the 5 by 5 grid. The table gives each column's original width and each row's original height. The area of a cell is its width times its row's height, and two totals start at 0: area covered by at least 1 rectangle, and by at least 2.
Row 0 has height 20, so its cell areas are [400, 400, 600, 200, 400] and its depths are [1, 1, 1, 0, 0]. Depth 1 or more adds 1400, depth 2 or more adds 0. The totals are now 1400 and 0.
Row 1 has height 10, so its cell areas are [200, 200, 300, 100, 200] and its depths are [1, 1, 2, 1, 1]. Depth 1 or more adds 1000, depth 2 or more adds 300. The totals are now 2400 and 300.
Row 2 has height 30, so its cell areas are [600, 600, 900, 300, 600] and its depths are [0, 0, 1, 1, 1]. Depth 1 or more adds 1800, depth 2 or more adds 0. The totals are now 4200 and 300.
Row 3 has height 20, so its cell areas are [400, 400, 600, 200, 400] and its depths are [0, 1, 2, 2, 1]. Depth 1 or more adds 1600, depth 2 or more adds 800. The totals are now 5800 and 1100.
Row 4 has height 20, so its cell areas are [400, 400, 600, 200, 400] and its depths are [0, 1, 1, 1, 0]. Depth 1 or more adds 1200, depth 2 or more adds 0. The totals are now 7000 and 1100.
All rows are summed. The area covered by at least one rectangle is 7000. The area covered by at least two is 1100; those cells are the ones marked Depth 2 or more.

The depths from the last figure sit on the 3 by 3 grid. The table gives each column's original width and each row's original height. The area of a cell is its width times its row's height, and two totals start at 0: area covered by at least 1 rectangle, and by at least 2.
Row 0 has height 20, so its cell areas are [400, 800, 800] and its depths are [1, 1, 1]. Depth 1 or more adds 2000, depth 2 or more adds 0. The totals are now 2000 and 0.
Row 1 has height 40, so its cell areas are [800, 1600, 1600] and its depths are [1, 2, 1]. Depth 1 or more adds 4000, depth 2 or more adds 1600. The totals are now 6000 and 1600.
Row 2 has height 40, so its cell areas are [800, 1600, 1600] and its depths are [1, 1, 1]. Depth 1 or more adds 4000, depth 2 or more adds 0. The totals are now 10000 and 1600.
All rows are summed. The area covered by at least one rectangle is 10000. The area covered by at least two is 1600; those cells are the ones marked Depth 2 or more.

The depths from the last figure sit on the 3 by 2 grid. The table gives each column's original width and each row's original height. The area of a cell is its width times its row's height, and two totals start at 0: area covered by at least 1 rectangle, and by at least 2.
Row 0 has height 20, so its cell areas are [1000, 1000] and its depths are [1, 0]. Depth 1 or more adds 1000, depth 2 or more adds 0. The totals are now 1000 and 0.
Row 1 has height 20, so its cell areas are [1000, 1000] and its depths are [1, 1]. Depth 1 or more adds 2000, depth 2 or more adds 0. The totals are now 3000 and 0.
Row 2 has height 20, so its cell areas are [1000, 1000] and its depths are [0, 1]. Depth 1 or more adds 1000, depth 2 or more adds 0. The totals are now 4000 and 0.
All rows are summed. The area covered by at least one rectangle is 4000. The area covered by at least two is 0; no cell has depth 2, so no cell is marked.
